conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be taking care of you tonight. Can you tell me what brought you to the hospital?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I’ve been seeing bright red blood when I go to the bathroom. A lot of it. And I feel weak, kind of dizzy.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. When did this start?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Couple days ago. I had it before, but it keeps coming back. I’ve had blood transfusions for it in the past.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. You also mentioned abdominal pain?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, it’s been going on for about a month. Starts in the lower right and left sides. Never really goes away.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Got it. We’re going to run some tests to check your blood and see if we can find the source of the bleeding.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I need another transfusion?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your hemoglobin is low at 7.3, so we’re giving you one unit of blood tonight to help with that.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my belly pain? It’s not getting better with the pills I’m on.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You were on oxycodone, right? We’re switching you to Dilaudid, which might work better for your pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, thanks. I just want to feel better.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We did a CT scan of your abdomen and pelvis. It didn’t show any active bleeding or serious issues like a blockage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So what’s causing the blood then?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Given your history of cirrhosis and the TIPS procedure, you could have bleeding from portal colopathy or varices. But hemorrhoids are also possible.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had that TIPS thing for a while. Shouldn’t that stop the bleeding?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It helps reduce pressure, but it doesn’t eliminate all risks. The scan did show your TIPS is still working well.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your blood cultures came back with no growth so far, which is good.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had infections before with my tubes. Should we check my urine?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your urine test showed signs of infection. We’re starting you on an antibiotic called cefepime because of past resistant bacteria.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I had Klebsiella before, right? That was tough to treat.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. You’re at higher risk, so we’re being cautious with the antibiotics.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: How’s your pain today?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: A little better since the new pain medicine. Still tired though.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your labs this morning show your kidney function is stable. Creatinine is 1.3, same as yesterday.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that bad?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s not great, but it’s not getting worse. You have chronic kidney disease, so we’re watching it closely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’re also holding your water pills—Lasix and spironolactone—for now because your kidneys are sensitive.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I don’t feel swollen, so that makes sense.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your hemoglobin dropped a bit to 7.1, but it’s stable overall. We’re not seeing signs of a fast bleed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So I’m not bleeding right now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s likely slow or intermittent. We still recommend an endoscopy, but it’s up to you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve had a lot of procedures. I’m thinking about leaving.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand, but there are risks. You could bleed more or get worse from the infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know. But I just want to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see you’ve decided to leave against medical advice. I want to make sure you understand the risks.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yeah, I could bleed to death. I get it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. Please keep taking the cefepime for the infection and follow up with your liver and urology doctors.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. And if I see more blood, I’ll come back.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s the best plan. Take care of yourself.
